summary: Top TJR clips (1M–4.2M views) are built on a single mechanism: ironic contrast delivered in the first 2 seconds, then resolved fast. The winning formula pairs an 'ordinary world' reference (graduation, peers, renting) against TJR's reality (Koenigsegg, cash, luxury lifestyle) using a blunt on-screen label, never a paragraph. Lifestyle and mindset moments dominate every platform; trading mechanics appear only as reaction fuel, never as explanation. Clips under 20 seconds dramatically outperform longer ones — the 4.2M view clip is 9.5 seconds, the 2.6M clip is 10.3 seconds. The caption is almost always one line or one word; the visual does all the explaining.
moments_to_pick: TJR delivering a short, quotable mindset or money line — especially anything about silence, not needing to explain himself, or rejecting the conventional path (e.g. college, 9-5, degree)
TJR physically with an exotic car, large cash sum, or expensive item — especially when a specific dollar figure is stated aloud or visible on screen
A moment where TJR's age or situation implicitly or explicitly contrasts with a 'normal' peer (mentioning classmates, graduation, same-age people doing ordinary things)
TJR reacting with visible joy, disbelief, or loud celebration to a big number, a purchase, or an unexpected win — face large, expressive, nothing ambiguous
TJR saying something self-aware or gently funny about his wealth, critics, or reputation — quotable, clean, zero anger
A milestone moment (trade hit, car delivered, big number crossed) where TJR's genuine emotional reaction is the whole story — joy or disbelief only
hook_examples: What does TJR do while they graduate?
He skipped the degree and bought THIS instead.
TJR just said something nobody could argue with. 👀
title_formula: Lead with TJR doing or saying one specific, concrete thing + a short emotional punchline or number. Under 60 characters. Pattern: 'TJR [specific action/quote] and [reaction or result]'. Never start with a question — lead with the fact, end with the tension. Example pattern (write original each time)
caption_formula: One punchy line only — either the exact quotable line from the clip, or a contrast statement framing TJR against the conventional path. No more than one sentence. One optional emoji at the end. Hard line break, then hashtags. Example structure: 'He doesn't explain himself. He just wins. 💸\n\n#tjr #t
avoid: Clips over 20 seconds — the data is unambiguous: 9.5s gets 4.2M, 10.3s gets 2.6M, 27.5s gets 1.9M, 25.3s gets 1.4M; every second over 20 bleeds retention
ALL CAPS subtitles — every million-view TJR clip uses sentence case; it reads cleaner and matches the calm-confidence tone of the brand
Captions longer than one sentence — the top posts use one line or one word maximum; paragraphs signal low-effort repost to the algorithm
Trading jargon (SPY, NQ, ES, calls, puts, full-porting, CPI) in titles or captions — 'Fullporting CPI' earned only 185K vs 1.55M for the lifestyle car clip; jargon caps the audience ceiling

Question-only titles with no concrete anchor — our own data shows the Nvidia clip (891 views) outperformed the vaguer Nasdaq hook (377 views) but both underperformed; the hook needs a specific fact, n
Clips that could read as mocking TJR, showing anger toward others, or framing him negatively — campaign rule and algorithmically penalised
